title: Quantum Fourier transform for the symmetric group
abstract: Quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) for general groups were recognized to be fundamental already early in the field. A canonical example of non-abelian QFT for the symmetric group was outlined by Beals (1997). Later, a more detailed analysis of this algorithm was carried out by Kawano and Sekigawa (2016). In this paper, we revisit that construction. After a careful analysis, we revise their gate complexity to $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{3.5})$ and circuit depth to $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^3)$. Moreover, we observe that their construction is not optimal in the choice of transversal elements, so we propose simpler realization of the symmetric group QFT.

bite.hook: Revised gate complexity down to tilde-O(n^3.5) for the quantum Fourier transform of the symmetric group.
tldr: Revisited the canonical symmetric group quantum Fourier transform construction by Kawano and Sekigawa.
Analyzed and revised the gate complexity to tilde-O(n^3.5) and circuit depth to tilde-O(n^3).
Proposed a simpler realization of the symmetric group QFT by optimizing the choice of transversal elements.
bite.whyItMatters: The quantum Fourier transform is a core subroutine for many quantum algorithms. Improving its complexity for complex mathematical groups helps make advanced quantum algorithms more feasible.
bite.eli5: Just like a regular computer uses fast math shortcuts to process audio frequencies, quantum computers use a special Fourier transform. Researchers just found a leaner, more efficient way to set up this math shortcut for complex symmetry groups.
